summary: The surface's private-authority regex has no left word boundary, unlike the controller's, so a controller-accepted dispatch rejection reason can still raise PrivateRunDisclosureError and latch work control UNCERTAIN.
failure_scenario: Hermes rejects a dispatch with reason 'Hermes cannot undeleg_x here' -> TaskDispatchOutcome accepts it (tasks.py:39-41 uses (?<![A-Za-z0-9])deleg_...) -> _settle_start builds WorkStartResult (work_tools.py:679, _validate_exact_text at :93) -> PrivateRunDisclosureError -> except BaseException at :757 marks health UNCERTAIN -> every later start/cancel returns 'work control unavailable; restart required'. Reachable only if the reason contains an embedded 'deleg_' token; contrived.
evidence: Ran in the project venv: TaskDispatchOutcome(task_id='task_1', accepted=False, reason='Hermes cannot undeleg_x here') constructs; WorkStartResult(accepted=False, state='rejected', task_id='task_1', reason=<same>) raises PrivateRunDisclosureError. Read the code paths; did not drive a full fake-session end-to-end run.

summary: Inbound sequence staleness is a global monotonic check, so cross-task ack and terminal reordering fails the whole controller.
failure_scenario: Task A's cancel or dispatch ack gets sequence 9 and task B's terminal gets sequence 10. If the terminal loop takes the controller lock first, B's terminal sets _max_inbound_sequence to 10, then A's ack (9, no reordered_after because A has no terminal or preack) hits 'inbound event sequence was stale' at :757 and _fail_locked poisons the controller, losing authority over all active tasks. The reorder allowance only covers a same-task terminal (_terminal_sequences or preack).
evidence: Code reading only: tasks.py:487-496, :635-638, :754-757, and the dispatch ack and terminal paths in integration/api.py (:1677, :1700, :1103). I did not construct a reproduction or show that the bridge delivers these out of order, so I could not confirm the race is reachable.

summary: tasks.py: dispatch fail-closed on uncertain ack (no re-dispatch; controller latched with _fail_locked), accepted/rejected ack evidence checks, preack terminal ordering, run-id binding at terminal settle, cancel keyed to exact task and expected run id, cancel and speech scopes not crossed. 4096-scalar completed-result limit uses len(str) (code points) with a separate surrogate check; the 1024 limit applies only to reasons and non-completed text.

task_proposals.py: proposal is consumed once before any projection or admission await; automatic path uses a unique invocation_id (automatic_<proposal_id>) so replay cannot double-dispatch. submit_for_ack returns the WorkStartResult from start_work, so a started claim follows the accepted ack. Confirmation needs a clean spoken capture or a typed card; stale, expired and mismatched-binding inputs refuse.

work_tools.py: invocation replay with the same semantics returns the existing binding; differing semantics marks UNCERTAIN. Duplicate-objective and capacity checks use pending plus active, and pending cancel-after-ack is handled under the lock. Residual unproven risk: _admit_binding_locked evicts the oldest completed binding once 256 invocations are reached, so a replay of an evicted invocation_id would re-dispatch unless the task is still active; I judged it too speculative to report.

companion/attestation.py and evidence/transport.py: attestation never raises and degrades to unknown/elsewhere; the RECORD read is bounded; transport is a Protocol only. scripts/benchmark_evidence_admission.py: validate_report recomputes aggregates, counts and thresholds and rejects mismatched pass flags; canonical JSON parsing rejects duplicates and non-canonical bytes. Schema files were only spot-checked (benchmark-machine and benchmark-report) and match the validators. The other four schemas were not examined. Benchmark timing, Windows-only native paths and the tests were not run, and I did not run the test suite.
